LESSON: MASS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six
Subject: MATHEMATICS FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: MEASUREMENT
Topic 2.4: Mass
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Mass, part of MEASUREMENT in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six MATHEMATICS FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How can we measure large amounts of mass?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Mass together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: Interacting with digital technology weighing machines to measure masses of different items.

● Critical thinking and problem solving: Active listening and communication in solving questions dealing with mass.

Values:
● Integrity: Consistency in determining mass of items in tonnes and kilograms using different operations involving

addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Environmental education: as learners discuss items in the environment such as loaded lorries, whose mass may be

measured in tonnes.

● Learner Support Programme: as a learner enhances peer education and mentorship to support one another in

identifying the relationship among cubic centimetres (cm3

), millilitres and litres practically.

38

Links to other Learning Areas:
Learner relates skills used for measuring to measurement in Science and Technology.

Suggested learning resources

● Teaspoon,

● soil/sand manual/electronic weighing machine and beam balance.

● Course books

● Signs dictionary
